policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The two perfect participles of ἵστημι are morphological variants of one form; ASV 'standing' is identical either way.
ASV reads only 'having his name, and the name of his Father'; there is no rendering of the added ἀριθμός ('number').
ASV 'they sing as it were a new song' renders ὡς; the omission would give simply 'a new song'.
English must supply a copula in 'These are they that were not defiled' whether or not εἰσιν stands in the Greek.
Subjunctive and indicative of ὑπάγω after ὅπου ἂν are both rendered 'whithersoever he goeth'.
ASV 'These were purchased from among men' has no agent phrase; the RP addition ὑπὸ Ἰησοῦ would require 'by Jesus'.
The readings differ only in word order and in how the shared ἐν … αὐτῶν phrase is displayed; ASV 'in their mouth was found no lie' fits all three.
ASV's clause 'they are without blemish' is asyndetic; the added γάρ would give 'for they are without blemish', and ASV renders the γάρ of v. 13.
ASV 'I saw another angel flying in mid heaven' renders ἄλλον.
εὐαγγελίσαι takes an accusative object with or without ἐπί; ASV 'to proclaim unto them that dwell' is the same either way.
ASV 'Fear God' renders θεόν; κύριον would give 'the Lord'.
ASV 'worship him that made' supplies the English antecedent 'him' under either the dative participle or the RP αὐτὸν τὸν ποιήσαντα.
The variant is the Greek article on θάλασσαν, which has no separate realization in ASV's 'and sea'.
Only the order of δεύτερος and ἄγγελος differs; ASV 'another, a second angel' does not preserve it.
ASV's doubled 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon' renders the repeated ἔπεσεν; the omission would give a single 'Fallen'.
ASV continues with the relative 'that hath made all the nations to drink', representing ἣ rather than starting a new independent clause.
The readings differ in article and word order only; ASV 'the holy angels' is identical either way.
ASV 'yea, saith the Spirit' excludes RP's λέγει Ναί order, but the base and r01 differ only in punctuation and have no distinct English.
Future indicative and aorist subjunctive of ἀναπαύω after ἵνα are both rendered 'that they may rest'.
ASV 'for their works follow with them' renders causal γάρ; δέ would give 'and' or be left unrendered.
The variant is the case of υἱός after ὅμοιον; ASV 'like unto a son of man' does not show it.
Genitive and accusative after ἐπί are both rendered 'on the cloud'.
ASV 'And another angel came out from the altar' renders the finite ἐξῆλθεν, which the Holmes base text lacks.
English 'he that hath power over fire' supplies its own head whether or not the Greek article stands.
ASV 'he called with a great voice' renders φωνῇ; κραυγῇ would give 'cry'.
